title: A content landing runs the contract lint on the articles it changes, so a CODE tag without a pointer cannot reach main
goal: backlog.py land runs .claude/skills/kb-verify/lint.py (or the same checks scoped to the changed articles) before sync --push when the landed range changes a kb root's articles, not only when it changes _tools/, so a lint error a worker's content commit adds stops that landing instead of the next code landing. Found by the SP-kyvu526t close: ST-umjb55sg's research landed three CODE tags with no path#symbol pointer (check.py and the content gate passed), and BG-2hjxwg64's landing stopped at its lint step until BG-oj3lixq2 fixed them.

run: import re,sys,pathlib;t=pathlib.Path('_tools/bl_land.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8');ok=bool(re.search(r'kb/[^\n]*lint|lint[^\n]*kb/',t));print('land names a lint step for kb article changes:',ok);sys.exit(int(not ok))

notes: Planning note: the check is a text probe that fails today (land runs LAND_HEAVY, which holds the lint, only when the range changes _tools/, bl_land.py:1210); a plan should replace it with a planted content landing whose pointerless CODE tag stops land at its lint step.
